title: The lint layers (L1-L13)
html:
English |

The lint layers (L1-L13)

golmet lint is the deterministic structural sweep of the kit, the engine config and the packs. It is read-only, never guesses, and carries the whole state — because the agent cannot: the lint loads everything, the agent fixes what it points. The cycle it enables: the lint detects → explains with a file, a line and a PT-BR remediation → the agent corrects → the lint confirms.

Where it runs: CI (the kit runs the lint against itself before any release), CLI (golmet lint) and MCP (gm_lint — the agent session sweeps and fixes). The maintenance skills also call it: gm-agent-health-monitor (structural health check), gm-setup (post-install validation), gm-workflow-improver (post-fix gate) and gm-pack-orchestrator (pack structure after publish/update).

Severity convention: error = breaks the contract or the render; warning = quality/UX drift that does not block flow.

The layers

Check Severity One-liner
L1 error dead references: path cited in backticks/link that exists in no known root
L3 warning orphans: config files with no provenance (manifest / personal / pack / allowlist / cited)
L4 error stale content-manifest entries (the file no longer exists on disk)
L5 warning structural names outside kebab-case ASCII
L6 error/warning ghost gm-* components cited that are not in the registry (error in sources; warning in historical docs)
L7 error folder structure outside the declared canonical tree (+ L7-size warnings for oversized single aggregates)
L8 warning definitives that lost the minimal structural skeleton declared by their kit templates
L9 error stack-templates registry schema (the materialized one and the org's in-pack registries)
L10 error/warning state-pack internals: rules without a trigger header, pattern types outside the EN taxonomy, domains/ without INDEX/KNOWLEDGE, working copy without pack.yaml
L11 warning broken or malformed Mermaid diagrams
L12 error (BOM = warning) encoding and broken text: non-UTF-8 bytes, U+FFFD, double-encoded accents, UTF-16/BOM
L13 warning language anchors: a PT-BR doc linking an EN destination when the PT counterpart exists on disk
L14 error front matter YAML parseable: an opening --- whose block fails YAML parsing (the unquoted X: Y value pattern)

L1 — dead references (error)

Every path cited in `backticks` or markdown links of the swept *.md files (kit sources/docs; AGENTS.md + profile/ of the config) must resolve in a known root (the file's dir, the kit root, the config root). Pack *.md files are NOT swept in v0.1 — pack business docs cite PRODUCT paths by design (a product repo's deploy.yml, for example), a structural false positive; pack-internal refs belong to L5/L7. Known false positives are handled with declared roots (profile/x resolves the kit-canonical coredata/rules/x; module-store refs and skills/<id> resolve against the registry).

Example finding: L1 AGENTS.md:6 — referência morta: `rules/client-profile.template.md` não existe → fix: point the citation at the right path (the template is emitted by golmet template client-profile — not stored in the config).

Tests: TestL1DeadRefsAndFalsePositives, TestL1RuntimeViewConfig, TestL1ContainerResolvesEngineConfigRoot.

L3 — orphans (warning)

Config files that no mechanism claims: not in the manifest, not personal-by-design, not inside a state pack, not on the declared orphan allowlist, not cited. The fix is a decision: move to the canonical place, designate personal-by-design, delete, or extend the declared orphan allowlist if it is a legitimate orphan.

Tests: TestL3OrphansWithAllowlistAndCited.

L4 — stale manifest entries (error)

A provenance entry in .golmet/manifest.json whose file no longer exists on disk. The kit removed or moved the file but the inventory kept the row — the classic signal after a refactor or an uninstall wave.

Example finding: L4 rules/packs/<pack-id>.md — entrada stale → fix: re-materialize (golmet pack update) or drop the stale entry.

Tests: TestL4ManifestStale.

L5 — names outside the pattern (warning)

Structural names (config first level, pack folders, skill dirs) outside kebab-case ASCII. Filenames with extensions are exempt; business content is not descended into.

Tests: TestL5NamesPTAndNonKebab.

L6 — ghost components (error in sources / warning in docs)

A gm-* mention that is not in the registry. Error in coredata/sources (the live contract), warning in docs (historical prose). The first real run caught ten misspelled component names across the kit sources (e.g. gm-task-spec → gm-taskspec) plus broken registry invokes.

Tests: TestL6GhostsByContext.

L7 — canonical structure (error) + L7-size (warning)

The declared canonical trees: the config root (agents/, skills/, profile/, packs/, plugins/, .golmet/, root settings), the state pack (pack.yaml + skills/ agents/ rules/ domains/ accumulation/ with accumulation/ restricted to patterns metrics nuances), the kit repo (coredata/ incl. templates/). Unknown dirs = findings; the fix is move or declare an exception.

L7-size warns when a workspace aggregate (DATA_MODEL, DECISIONS, ERROR_CATALOG, GLOSSARY) grows past the declared split thresholds — the lint detects without grammar; the split plan belongs to gm-doc.

Tests: TestL7CanonicalStructure, TestL7TemplateDepositFlag, TestL7SpecAggregatesUnitaryAndBroken, TestL7SizeWarningsEarlyCandidates, TestL7L1Container.

L8 — definitives vs. templates (warning)

The config's definitives (AGENTS.md, the profiles) must keep the minimal structural skeleton their kit templates declare: the marker blocks, the canonical sections. Extra content is legitimate evolution (never a finding); only structural loss flags. Definitive absent (fresh machine before setup) = silent skip; a template deposited into the config = L7 warning (templates live in the kit — M12).

Tests: TestL8StructuralConformance, TestL7TemplateDepositFlag.

L9 — stack-templates registry schema (error)

Both registries the reader consumes (the kit-materialized profile/stack-templates.yaml and the org's in-pack packs/*/rules/stack-templates.yaml — pack-first, M15) must parse as YAML with the minimal schema: boilerplate_org present, every template with detect, description present when boilerplate is set.

Tests: TestL9StackTemplatesSchema, TestL9PackRegistrySchema.

L10 — state-pack internals (error/warning)

Inside packs/<id>/ state packs: rules/*.md without an explicit trigger header (the gm-rule-keeper format: H1 + "> Gatilho: AO ...", one norm per file), pattern folders outside the EN taxonomy (process|architecture|code|ui|test|data), domains/ without INDEX or domains/<domain>/ without KNOWLEDGE, and a working copy carrying .git without pack.yaml (error — the pack's source of truth is gone). The lint points; the canonical writer corrects (gm-rule-keeper, gm-pattern-extractor, gm-domain-research).

Tests: TestL10PackState and siblings.

L11 — Mermaid diagrams (warning)

Deterministic heuristic, no Node: valid diagram type on the first significant line (declared list), balanced delimiters per block (the ER attribute-block pattern opens { on one line and closes on another — judging per line breaks valid syntax), quoted labels in pairs, arrows with both ends, subgraph/end pairing, closed fence. Broken Mermaid fails the render silently (the viewer shows raw code) — the lint makes it loud.

Tests: TestL11Mermaid.

L12 — encoding and broken text (error; BOM = warning)

Text broken by encoding is invisible in structure and only breaks at render: non-UTF-8 bytes (Latin-1/Windows-1252 saved raw), replacement character U+FFFD (the content is already corrupted in the file), double-encoded accents (the classic "Ã©/Ã£/Ã§" pairs — UTF-8 read as Latin-1 and re-saved), UTF-16 BOM (error), UTF-8 BOM (warning — IMP-096: no BOM). evals are excluded (fixtures may carry intentional content).

Tests: TestL12Encoding.

L13 — language anchors (warning)

A link in a *.pt-br.md doc pointing an EN destination when the PT counterpart exists on disk. The real find: the PT README navigating into EN docs — the link resolved in L1 but taught the wrong language. Only PT docs are validated (an EN base linking a PT counterpart is legitimate: badge, cross-links). The remediation swaps to the PT counterpart and warns to check the #section anchor in the new language.

Tests: TestL13Anchors.

L14 — front matter YAML parseable (error)

A *.md file whose front matter block (opening --- on the first line, closed by the next ---) fails YAML parsing (gopkg.in/yaml.v3). The real find: a value containing a colon-plus-space (X: Y) written unquoted — the parser reads it as a nested mapping ("Nested mappings are not allowed in compact mappings") and every YAML consumer of the doc fails with it. Quote the whole value with double quotes. Files without a front-matter opener skip silently; a lone --- stays a legitimate horizontal rule.

Tests: TestL14FrontMatter.

The anti-false-positive policy

A finding that flags valid content trains people to ignore the lint. Every heuristic follows: ffalse-positive is worse than false-negative. The proof ran on L11's first day: three real false positives (per-line delimiters vs. the ER attribute-block pattern, the erDiagram cardinality tokens, the sequenceDiagram alt...end blocks) were caught on the first sweep and turned into heuristic fixes plus regression tests. Declared allowlists and per-check heuristics live in the FORMAT §9.1 and in code.

The normative contract

The checks enforce FORMAT §9.1 — the lint is the executor, the FORMAT is the contract. Reference: commands (golmet lint) and tools (gm_lint).
